successors.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
successors.text: 'Tiglath-Pileser III attacked Damascus and annexed Aram'; the population was deported and Rezin executed

ledger.x: c. 1100 BCE: the kingdom of Aram-Damascus arises at Damascus. The page says the polity 'existed from the late 12th century BCE to 732 BCE'; it names no founder and no founding act.
842 BCE (bridged): Hazael's wars take Israelite Transjordan.

c. 830 BCE (bridged): Hazael besieges and takes Gath. 'Recent excavations at Tell es-Safi/Gath have revealed dramatic evidence of the siege and subsequent conquest of Gath by Hazael'; the year mirrors the philistia dossier's c. 830, which rests on a page not opened here. Hazael's reign (842-796)…
c. 830 BCE (bridged): the raid on Gath ends in the same year; no occupation of the Philistine coast is recorded on the page, and Gath stays Philistine in the philistia dossier.
796 BCE (bridged): Hazael dies and the Israelite Transjordan contest ends.
732 BCE: the kingdom of Aram-Damascus ends with Rezin, its last king (754-732 BCE).

wars.name: Battle of Qarqar and Shalmaneser III's campaigns against Damascus
wars.outcome: Assyrian claim of victory at Qarqar in 853 BC; 'Shalmaneser's opponents held on to their thrones after this battle' and the coalition's king Hadadezer remained king of Damascus until at least 841 BC.

wars.name: Hazael's wars against Israel and Philistia
wars.outcome: Hazael 'seized Israelite territory east of the Jordan River', took Gath and 'sought to take Jerusalem' without success; Israel recovers after his death.

wars.name: Syro-Ephraimite War
wars.outcome: Rezin and Pekah's invasion of Judah (735 BCE) fails; Assyria annexes Aram-Damascus and 'much of Levant' by 732.

certainty.note: No boundary of Aram-Damascus is described on any page opened; the southern edge with Ammon and the western edge with Israel are approximate.
